children: Heineken looks to be making moves to bolster control over its future sales growth, analysts at J.P. Morgan write. The world's second-largest brewer is focusing on dynamics beyond its core beer category, such as zero-alcohol products, and is looking for ways to capture growth across more premium areas and developed markets, JPM says, citing comments made by finance chief Harold van den Broek this week. "The group increasingly targets the total landscape of consumer needs rather than beer alone," the bank says. JPM has a neutral rating and a 70-euro target on the Amsterdam-listed stock. (joshua.kirby@wsj.com; @joshualeokirby)
